messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: 30 mg of furosemide over the first hour, then 12.5 mg per hour for the subsequent 4 hours.
This dose is delivered automatically by the On-Body Infusor.
The device must be applied by a healthcare provider or adult caregiver.
This applies to children weighing at least 43 kg.
Furoscix is not for chronic use.
It should be replaced with oral diuretics as soon as practical.
People with significantly reduced kidney function may need additional diuretic therapy.
Both Furoscix devices deliver a fixed 80 mg dose.
The therapy is needed because both Furoscix devices deliver a fixed 80 mg dose.
Usual adult furosemide dose for pulmonary edema:
IV: 40 mg IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes.
If a satisfactory response does not occur within one hour.
A satisfactory response may be increased to 80 mg.
The response is administered IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes.
Use: adjunctive therapy in acute pulmonary edema.
IV administration is indicated when a rapid onset of diuresis is desired.
Usual adult furosemide dose for hypertension:
Oral: initial dose 80 mg/day, usually divided into 40 mg orally twice a day.
Triples: [["Furosemide", "has recommended dose", "30 mg over the first hour, then 12.5 mg per hour for the subsequent 4 hours"], ["Furosemide", "administered via", "On-Body Infusor"], ["On-Body Infusor", "must be applied by", "healthcare provider or adult caregiver"], ["Furosemide", "recommended for", "children weighing at least 43 kg"], ["Furoscix", "not for", "chronic use"], ["Furoscix", "should be replaced with", "oral diuretics as soon practical"], ["Furosemide", "has administration instruction", "people with significantly reduced kidney function may need additional diuretic therapy"], ["Furoscix", "has fixed dose", "80 mg"], ["Furosemide", "has administration instruction", "therapy is needed because both Furoscix devices deliver a fixed 80 mg dose"], ["Furosemide", "has recommended dose", "40 mg IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes"], ["Furosemide", "has administration instruction", "if a satisfactory response does not occur within one hour"], ["Furosemide", "has recommended dose", "80 mg"], ["Furosemide", "administered via", "IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes"], ["Furosemide", "used in", "adjunctive therapy in acute pulmonary edema"], ["Furosemide", "has administration instruction", "IV administration is indicated when a rapid onset of diuresis is desired"], ["Furosemide", "has recommended dose", "80 mg/day"], ["Furosemide", "has administration instruction", "oral: initial dose 80 mg/day, usually divided into 40 mg orally twice a day"]]
Relations: ["administered via", "has administration instruction", "has fixed dose", "has recommended dose", "must be applied by", "not for", "recommended for", "should be replaced with", "used in"]
Answer:

completion:
administered via: The subject drug is delivered or administered using the method or device specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug has a specific guideline or instruction related to its use, as specified by the object entity.  
has fixed dose: The subject device or drug delivers a predetermined, unchanging dose specified by the object entity.  
has recommended dose: The subject drug has a specific dosage recommendation specified by the object entity.  
must be applied by: The subject device requires the specified entity to apply or use it.  
not for: The subject drug or device is not intended for the condition or use specified by the object entity.  
recommended for: The subject drug is recommended for use in patients with the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.  
should be replaced with: The subject drug or device should be replaced with the treatment or medication specified by the object entity.  
used in: The subject drug is used as part of the therapeutic approach or treatment specified by the object entity.
